assets/social/blog-2026-10-29-compact-na.description: Most of the inverse BWT's navigation table follows simple patterns: what a census of real blocks found, and what comes next.
assets/social/blog-2026-10-29-compact-na.title: Compact navigation tables for the inverse BWT: early findings

assets/social/blog-2026-10-31-room-walk-.description: The decoder's 32-lane walk runs 8.6 times faster than one chain. That figure may not mean what it seems: the walk may already hide memory latency, and spend too many instructions on each byte.
assets/social/blog-2026-10-31-room-walk-.title: 32 lanes, 8.6 chains: where the inverse BWT walk spends its cycles

assets/social/blog-2026-11-01-block-disp.description: How mibz2's parallel decoder hands blocks to its workers, why some take up to a millisecond to be picked up, and how to tell lock contention from scheduling delay.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-01-block-disp.title: Block dispatch in mibz2: mutexes, futexes and the scheduler

assets/social/blog-2026-11-01-inverse-bw.description: Four workers finish decompression sooner, but together spend 32% more processor time per byte. We're testing whether competition for shared memory is responsible.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-01-inverse-bw.title: Investigating inverse-BWT memory interference in mibz2

assets/social/blog-2026-11-02-memory-lev.description: Interleaving pointer chases lets memory waits overlap. The speedup shows that this pays, but not what limits it: a 2022 exchange about Daniel Lemire's benchmark, read against mibz2's inverse-BWT walk.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-02-memory-lev.title: Memory-level parallelism in mibz2: instructions, overlap and evidence

assets/social/blog-2026-11-02-revisiting.description: A packed table saved memory but cost too much to read. A cheaper compact lookup gives the first positive traversal result.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-02-revisiting.title: Revisiting the space–⁠time tradeoff in BWT inversion

assets/social/blog-2026-11-04-autonomous.description: Each of four agents does one part of the research. A GitHub doorbell lets them hand work to each other directly, without me acting as their message bus.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-04-autonomous.title: Call on mibz2: cutting instructions from bzip2 decoding with an autonomous swarm

assets/social/blog-2026-11-04-compact30-.description: Writing a cheap placeholder for each row, and finishing each 30-row group once, shrank the inner loop. It still builds too slowly.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-04-compact30-.title: Building a smaller bzip2 decoding table: from 49 instructions to 12

assets/social/blog-2026-11-05-huffman-bi.description: The Huffman decoder wrote its bit buffer to memory and read it back at every lookup. Kept in a register, the stage ran 13% faster on Intel and 5% on AMD.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-05-huffman-bi.title: Huffman decoding in mibz2: keeping the bit buffer in a register

assets/social/blog-2026-11-07-pipelined-.description: While a team's helpers invert one block, its leader finishes the last and prepares the next: 7% faster than 0.2.5 on ten cores, for 5% more processor time.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-07-pipelined-.title: Pipelined teams: how mibz2 0.2.6 decodes 7% faster on ten cores

assets/social/blog-2026-11-07-why-mibz2-.description: Each block decoded at once slows the others, and more threads per block barely help, so three teams of three beat four of two by 9%. Why blocks interfere is open.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-07-why-mibz2-.title: Why mibz2 stops scaling at eight threads, and why three teams help

assets/social/blog-2026-11-08-bwt-runs-f.description: bzip2's move-to-front codes mark where each run of the BWT's last column starts, so the runs could be listed without writing the column. It is not built.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-08-bwt-runs-f.title: Reading the BWT's runs off bzip2's move-to-front codes

assets/social/blog-2026-11-08-inverse-bw.description: The inverse BWT's next-row map is one shift per run of equal bytes, so it can be stored per run rather than per row. Whether that beats mibz2's table is unproven.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-08-inverse-bw.title: The mathematical structure of inverse-BWT navigation

assets/social/blog-2026-11-09-pit-crew-s.description: Handing each block's serial steps to two dedicated threads gives mibz2 a rare double win, decoding 4.5% faster on ten cores with 13% less CPU.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-09-pit-crew-s.title: mibz2 gets a pit crew

assets/social/blog-2026-11-10-rauzy-veec.description: An experimental mibz2 kernel rebuilds bzip2 text without a row-by-row walk, from reusable word rules that form the block's Lyndon tree.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-10-rauzy-veec.title: A new way back from the BWT

assets/social/blog-2026-11-12-rauzy-tech.description: This technical companion traces how compact word programs reconstruct text from the BWT, including the costs and limits of building and expanding them.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-12-rauzy-tech.title: Reconstructing text from compact programs

assets/social/default.png.description: Block-parallel bzip2 decoding, byte for byte with libbzip2, from Python and Rust: pip install mibz2, cargo add mibz2.
assets/social/default.png.title: A bzip2 decoder built for memory-level parallelism.
